- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via DatasourceConnectionService (symbol, a top-level class), IDataEngine (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `358cc92507e5ef8f769a799bf611cc06a56626c8` — the merge of head `a5f0c8b5dcab727e54d4728c6b3f921b0e0bc903` into base `968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 358cc92507e5ef8f769a799bf611cc06a56626c8 && git checkout 358cc92507e5ef8f769a799bf611cc06a56626c8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925 a5f0c8b5dcab727e54d4728c6b3f921b0e0bc903 && git checkout -B drift-repro 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925 && git merge --no-ff a5f0c8b5dcab727e54d4728c6b3f921b0e0bc903

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **先看：** `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts`（`reconnect` 开头的拒绝分支）、`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`（`listDatasourceDefs`）、`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`（两处文档）。

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts` (hits) — judged against the ruling it implements (card #27727 Task 1-2, filed off 6508089206 ④ should-fix 1-2, which asked that the member doc carry the exception and that the read-back either answer `driver` or say it omits it), against its implementer (`ObjectQL.registerDatasourceDef` :9250-9262, `listDatasourceDefs` :9320-9327) and against its first consumers (`DatasourceConnectionService.attemptConnect` :673-678 and `reconnect.restoreOldPool` :869-877, which write through `registerDatasourceDef?`; `secret-reference-union.ts` :598-623, which reads `listDatasourceDefs?`):

- The member doc now states the one exception the engine actually has. Read in the implementer: `const driver = def.driver ?? this.datasourceDefs.get(def.name)?.driver` then `set(name, { driver, schemaMode: def.schemaMode, external: def.external })` — every key but `driver` IS last-write-wins (an absent `schemaMode` or `external` overwrites with `undefined`), and `driver` alone keeps. The doc says exactly that and no more. Holds.
- The key doc's new claim, "`listDatasourceDefs` answers the stored id", holds against the only implementation in the tree: :9323 spreads `driver` when defined, and the spread order keeps `name` first and `driver` before `schemaMode`, so a definition that never named one is still listed without the key (pinned at external-driver-floor.test.ts :612-616). Tried to break it on both entry routes the `listDatasourceDefs?` doc names: the manifest path (`registerApp` :8648 calls `registerDatasourceDef(ds)` with the manifest datasource, whose `driver` rides along; pinned :603-611) and the member path (pinned :591-602, including the KEPT id after a driver-less re-registration). A sweep asking "which datasources name a plugin driver" can now be typed against the contract and answered by the engine. Holds.
- The doc-link direction is the right one: the key doc points at the read-back member, the member doc points at the key. The `listDatasourceDefs?` member doc itself (:480-500) still describes the answer in terms of `credentialsRef` and says nothing of `driver`. Not a contradiction (it says UNFILTERED, every definition, fresh copies) — a nit, no gate: one clause there naming `driver` as an answered key would make the read-back doc self-contained for the sweep author who starts from the member, not from the key.
- The "deliberate SUBSET" header rule holds: no key is added; the engine reads every key the contract declares.
- No must-fix on this file. No should-fix on this file.

Narrowing face — `DatasourceConnectionService.reconnect` requires `previous` (every non-prose path read), judged against the published spec on `main` (the method as `@objectstack/service-datasource` exports it, where `previous` was optional and its doc already said the kept-pool restore needs it) and against the scenario the card accepts it for (a host calling `reconnect` without `previous` after an eviction gets a kept plugin pool restored under a def naming no driver, served unfloored, silently):

- Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer? Yes, one: a `reconnect` call without `previous`. On `main` that call was never a correct call for a plugin driver (the restore registered `driver: undefined`, and after `unregisterDriver` dropped the stored def there was nothing to keep — the engine comment at :9254-9258 says so in as many words), so what is removed is the way to reach the defect, not a working path. Declared with the BREAKING banner and the one-line fix. RIGHT.
- Does it make the spec's own refusal real? Yes: the method's own doc on `main` already said the restore "must restore the def the old pool was serving under"; a call that cannot name that def's driver is now refused instead of being honoured wrongly. RIGHT.
- Tried to break the guard in the live code:
